architecture.title: How a results table is made, and where it is read
architecture.caption: The loop (Propose–Probe–Compose with a library) runs inside each stream and never sees a score. bench.judge scores each task's final deliverable after its step. Three streams in shuffled order give three means; the reading rule asks whether all three paired differences agree and whether the gap clears one SD. A promoted version is a different protocol: a fixed tree on the frozen test half, three trials, pass^3. (Protocol as reported in the paper; reading rule as the course's pre-registered criteria, EXAMPLE design, Module 09.)

sequence.title: Reading one row: generic editor vs Harness² k=1 on sim-cloud
sequence.caption: Captured from Lab 06-2 (SIM). The three paired stream differences are −2.4, −4.1 and −3.2: all agree. The gap of 3.2 is larger than the larger SD (2.9). The row reads 'beyond noise'. The same arm on sim-local reads 'beyond noise' too: −4.6 / −6.8 / −10.1, a gap of 7.2 against a larger SD of 4.3.

charts.title: pass@3 vs pass^3 for base v1 on sim-cloud (test half)
charts.caption: From Lab 06-3, SIM, captured on this Mac (seed 0). The formula assumes independent trials; observed pass^3 is higher because one task's trials are correlated. A worked example: 75% per trial gives about 42% across three trials.
